text:
lucy_support: FYI customer (acme-ml) opened an escalation — p95/p99 for streaming endpoints jumped ~2x since yesterday, non-streaming looks stable. They see big TTFB spikes and then normal chunking once stream starts.

devon: which model / route?

lucy_support: model redwood/llama-xl-compat, route /v1/stream with SSE. Observed in 3 regions: us-west, eu, ap-south. Attached repro steps below.

mike_ops: can you paste a quick repro curl? I can run against edge.

lucy_support: sure — curl they used (sanitized):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"model":"llama-xl-compat","input":"long prompt ~1k tokens","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```

lucy_support: customer says first byte delay spikes to 1.2s at p95 (was ~300ms yesterday), but total time for full completion unchanged.

devon: that screams first-chunk/flush/coalescing. Any proxy churn or nginx/h2 changes in last 24h?

infra-bot: deploy: infra/proxy 2026-03-13T02:18Z rolled to canary -> prod 2026-03-14T01:05Z (change: enable http2 write coalescing optimization).

sara: ah — we enabled a coalesce optimization on the HTTP/2 path to reduce small writes. Good for throughput but could increase TTFB for streaming.

mike_ops: any traces for a slow request?

tracing-bot: trace link: https://traces.internal/trace/9a7f... (p95 span shows edge-proxy wait 820ms before first send)

devon: that matches. Proxy holding onto small SSE frames to coalesce. Should not affect non-streamed responses because they buffer then send. For streaming we need low-latency flush.

lucy_support: customer reproduced with direct backend (bypassing proxy) and saw p95 ~320ms, so proxy is likely culprit.

mike_ops: low-risk mitigation: roll back coalescing toggle on edge for streaming routes or add per-route bypass header. We can ship a quick config to disable coalescing for /v1/stream.

sara: config snippet (env var on proxy):
```
HTTP2_COALESCE_ENABLED=true
# per-route override
route.metadata["streaming"] = "no-coalesce"
```

devon: alternative: reduce coalesce window from 50ms -> 5ms for streaming routes (less throughput win but better TTFB). Which do we prefer for now?

mike_ops: do per-route override and also push 5ms global fallback. Plan: roll per-route bypass to canary in us-west now, monitor p95, then prod.

lucy_support: customer is on us-west primarily. I'll ask them to validate canary edge endpoint once we flip it.

infra-bot: action: created ticket PROXY-4121 "disable http2 coalescing for streaming routes" assigned to mike_ops.

tracing-bot: note: also saw occasional reordering where first SSE event delivered, then a 200ms gap, then rest — suggests batch timer + OS socket buffer interplay.

devon: checklist for post-mitigation:
- revert/hotfix per-route metadata to bypass coalesce
- push 5ms coalesce window global
- add metric: first-chunk-latency per-route (p50/p95/p99) with proxy tag
- update runbook: if streaming TTFB regression -> check proxy coalesce flag + canary history

sara: added runbook fragment to ticket. Also note: we should validate clients that multiplex HTTP/2 properly (some client libraries want full buffer fill before exposing data). Customer is using node-fetch on older runtime — might be partially compounding.

lucy_support: customer testing canary now — they reported initial drop to p95 ~360ms (from 1.2s). They said still slightly higher than baseline but much better.

mike_ops: monitor for 30m, if stable roll to prod. Also open a follow-up to add explicit SSE flush header from runtime when chunk ready (STREAM_FLUSH_HINT) so proxy can treat writes as flush-worthy.

devon: good. also capture TCP traces for a couple samples to ensure Nagle/TCP_CORK not adding skew.

lucy_support: leaving customer on the canary edge and updating them every 15m. Will close once prod roll and they confirm. :thumbsup:

mike_ops: ETA for prod roll ~45m if canary looks good.

infra-bot: deployment scheduled: canary -> prod in 45m if no alert.

lucy_support: summary for ticket notes: streaming TTFB p95 regression due to http2 write coalescing optimization on proxy. Mitigation: per-route bypass + reduce coalesce window; add metrics and runbook updates; client runtime note.

sara: add postmortem if customer SLA impacted.

lucy_support: will follow up.

mike_ops: thanks all — nice catch."
